Cooking Converter

Cups, spoons and milliliters — plus grams via ingredient density.

–
Weight (grams)
UnitVolume

Gram weights use typical ingredient densities, so they are estimates. 1 US cup = 236.588 ml.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the amount in the first field.
  2. Pick the volume unit you are converting from.
  3. Choose the ingredient to apply its density.
  4. Read the volume in every unit plus the estimated weight in grams.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Which units and ingredients are supported?

Cups, tablespoons, teaspoons, fluid ounces, milliliters and liters. Volume is converted first, then multiplied by the ingredient's density to get grams.

How accurate are the gram weights?

Densities are typical averages (e.g. all-purpose flour ≈ 0.53 g/ml). Brands and packing vary, so treat the gram weight as an estimate, not a lab measurement.

How many milliliters are in a cup?

1 US cup = 236.588 ml. Note that some countries use a 250 ml metric cup.
